#### **Aim :**
To create two vectors in R—one of size 5 containing the value 2 and another of size 4 containing the value 5, combine them into a single vector, add an element with value 1, and extract the elements present at odd positions.

#### **Theory :**
In R, a **vector** is a collection of elements of the same data type. The `rep()` function is used to create vectors with repeated values, while the `c()` function combines multiple vectors. Elements can be added to a vector using `c()`, and specific elements can be extracted using **indexing**. Odd-position elements can be selected using a sequence of indices such as `seq(1, length(value), by = 2)`.

#### **Problem :**
Generate one vector of size 5 with each entry as 2 and second vector of size 4 with each entry as 5 and perform the following tasks :
```{r}
# Generating the vectors
v1 <- rep(2, 5)
cat("The vector of size 5 with each entry as 2 :",v1)
v2 <- rep(5, 4)
cat("The vector of size 4 with each entry as 5 :",v2)
```
**I.** Combine them into a single vector
```{r}
# Combining the vector
combined <- c(v1, v2)
cat("The combined vector is :",combined)
```
**II.** Add an element to combined vector, whose value is 1 and store them into another vector.
```{r}
additional <- c(combined, 1)
cat("The vector after adding an additional elements :",additional)
```
**III.** Extract all the elements which are at the odd places.
```{r}
# Extracting all elements at odd places
odd_places <- additional[seq(1, length(additional), by = 2)]
cat("The elements which are at odd places :",odd_places)
```

#### **Result :**
The two vectors were successfully created and combined. An element with value 1 was added, and the elements at odd positions were successfully extracted.
